title: Chapter 13: Blessing or Curse?
html:
Chen Ge stared at the screen with absolute concentration. The wheel gradually slowed until the pointer stopped on one result.

“Lucky Spin completed. Congratulations on winning a Rare Special Item: Cursed Love Letter (Chance of Winning: 3/1000!)

“After her death, the pale-faced girl became a taboo subject at the school. In red dancing shoes and a bloodstained uniform, even her name was spoken only in frightened whispers. Everyone pretended she had never existed—until one day, someone began receiving her love letters again.

“A Baleful Specter obtained on your first Lucky Spin. Rare Title unlocked: The Specters’ Favored.

“The Specters’ Favored: While this title is equipped, there is a chance that specters will offer you their help.”

The information on the screen made Chen Ge’s head spin.Cursed Love Letter? A three-in-a-thousand chance? The Specters’ Favored? I haven’t even dealt with the thing in the mirror, and now I’ve picked up another supernatural problem. I genuinely can’t tell whether I’m lucky or cursed.

He regretted jinxing himself before spinning the wheel. Chen Ge, get a grip. This still isn’t the worst possible outcome. Drawing a Baleful Specter doesn’t mean it will appear immediately. Maybe there’s still time to fix this. Perhaps I should burn some incense at the nearby temple.

He pocketed the phone, and his fingers brushed something papery inside his pocket. Looking down, he was startled to see the corner of a yellowed letter sticking out. A bad feeling settled in his stomach as he carefully pulled it free. Only one short sentence appeared on the page, its letters formed from strands of hair: “I like you.”

What the f*ck! Please tell me what you like about me, and I promise I’ll change it immediately!

The letters had graceful curves; under any other circumstances, the handwriting might even have looked beautiful.

Standing in the West House with the letter in both hands, Chen Ge muttered, “Who would’ve thought the first love letter I ever received would be something like this…”

“Boss! What are you muttering about in here?” Xiao Wan came up behind him after finishing the reset in the Main House.

“Nothing. I was just thinking—if someone knew he might not have much time left, should he stop chasing money and focus on leaving something meaningful behind?” Chen Ge looked up at Xiao Wan, still wearing her corpse makeup. “You know, help people, start a family, leave some kind of legacy.”

Chen Ge was only rambling, but Xu Wan seemed to take the question seriously. Her expression grew thoughtful.

“Xiao Wan, don’t tell me you’re actually considering that last part? Thanks, but I’m not ready yet. Then again, we’ve worked together for a long time and we do make a good team. I suppose if you insisted, I might not say no…” For some reason, Chen Ge suddenly felt nervous.

“No, Boss, that’s not it. I’m just wondering why you have two shadows following you.” Xu Wan pointed behind him. “Is this some new effect you came up with?”

“Two shadows?!” Chen Ge whipped around and saw two shadows, one large and one small, stretching behind him. As he watched, they slowly merged into one. “What the f*ck!”

He immediately grabbed Xu Wan and hurried out of the Haunted House.

Only when sunlight touched his skin did Chen Ge finally relax. Without explaining anything to Xu Wan, he sank onto the steps.

“Boss, you’ve been acting strange lately. Is it the financial pressure?” Xu Wan sat beside him. “Don’t worry. I’m sure things will work out. Anyway, what do you want for lunch? I’ll pick something up for you.”

Hearing Xu Wan try to comfort him, Chen Ge did not know how to respond. He forced a smile. “I’ll have whatever you’re having. Just remember to remove your makeup before you go, or you might frighten the cafeteria staff.”

“Understood.”

After Xu Wan left, Chen Ge pulled out the love letter again. I saw those two shadows merge with my own eyes. If that means the specter is haunting me, could it be hiding inside my shadow?

Chen Ge stared fixedly at his shadow. The Specters’ Favored gives me a chance to receive help from specters. Looked at that way, drawing a Baleful Specter might not be quite as bad as I thought.

That, at least, was what Chen Ge tried to tell himself. Deep down, he knew Baleful Specters earned their name because they were born from intense anguish and carried powerful curses. One careless mistake around such a thing could easily be fatal.

After lunch, Chen Ge stood outside the Haunted House handing out flyers. Plenty of people were visiting the park, but none seemed willing to enter his attraction.

Bored, Chen Ge opened the video-sharing app and found several new private messages. He deleted the trolling and advertisements, then personally replied to the rest. Before long, he came across a message from He San.

The earnest young man had contacted him privately to say that their university forum was exploding. After learning that the Haunted House had frightened one of the most admired girls in their department, many students declared that they wanted to come challenge the place themselves. Someone had even started organizing a group, and volunteers were already piling in.

“It’s good to be young.” Chen Ge smiled. In his mind, however, he could already picture a group of overconfident students huddled together and trembling inside his Haunted House.

“After completing the Trial Mission, I’ll have them try it out to see how scary the 1-star scenario really is.”

The thought of the Trial Mission made Chen Ge serious again. He had only one chance to complete it; failure would permanently cost him the opportunity to unlock the scenario. He reviewed the mission details until he had memorized everything available.

Know your enemy and half the battle is won. After confirming the mission location, the first thing Chen Ge did was search online for everything he could find about the place.

“Ping An Apartments, western countryside of Jiujiang City.”

Searching the location name turned up nothing at first. After digging through several pages of results, Chen Ge finally found a reference to the apartment complex on a secondhand property website.

It was a complaint accusing a seller of hiding the property’s history. According to the post, the apartment was genuinely haunted: beneath the fresh paint were old, suspicious stains, and at night a persistent foul odor filled the building.

No one had replied to the complaint, and it had quickly been buried beneath newer threads. The post was dated nine months earlier.

Spending the night in a haunted apartment while looking for a hidden murderer… Sigh. This is harder than I expected.Chen Ge had studied toy design; when it came to investigations or genuinely dangerous situations, he was a complete amateur. The hard part isn’t spending the night there. It’s what happens if the person I’m looking for is staying nearby and comes after me in the middle of the night.
